events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.93)
events.body:
The case enters the NS framework through NS-0: the driver cancelled (F3) and he claims a rider no-show (F11, F12), so the fee's validity is tested by NS-1. [F3][F11][F12][NS-0]

NS-1(i) is satisfied on the record — the timeline shows a driver "I'm Here" tap at 22:37:10 (F5) — but (ii) and (iii) fail. At the moment of the tap the driver was 1000 m from the pickup point (F5), and across the whole trip his closest approach was 868 m (F1), with the platform never recording an arrival (F4). His stationary period of 5 min 5 s was at 993 m from the pickup (F2), and the time he spent inside the 200 m radius after the tap was 0 s (F5). The three NS-1 conditions are cumulative, so the $6.61 no-show fee never became payable. [F1][F2][F4][F5][NS-1]

Because NS-1 fails, NS-2 governs and directs a full refund of the $6.61. The fee amount is taken from the fare record (F7, charged per F3); this is an entitlement dispute, not a billing error, but the entitlement is absent. [F3][F7][NS-1][NS-2]

The driver's chat message "I'm here already ... please come out" at 22:37 (F9) and his written statement that he waited more than three minutes at the pickup (F12) are both contradicted by the GPS and timeline records (F5, F2, F1, F4); system records override statements, and the rider's reply that she was at the pickup point and saw no car (F10) is consistent with those records. [F9][F10][F12][F1][F2][F4][F5][NS-1]

On the account action: the trace records an "I'm Here" tap while GPS placed the driver outside the pickup range (F5, F1), which is exactly the abuse-of-the-cancellation/waiting-button branch that NS-2 attaches `flag_account` to. The driver's two upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F17) do not decide this case — profile facts never decide a case and RD-6 only supplies the accompanying account action — but they reinforce that the flag, not the refund, is where the 90-day history bites. The flag is therefore attached alongside the refund. [F1][F5][F17][NS-2][RD-6]

What would change this ruling: Had NS-1 (ii) held ((ii) within 200 m of pickup AT THE MOMENT of the tap), the fee would stand and no refund would be due. | Had NS-1 (iii) held ((iii) stayed at the pickup > 3 min after the tap, until cancelling), the fee would stand and no refund would be due.

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We reviewed your dispute and you're getting a full refund of the $6.61 cancellation fee. It's paid as a Ryde voucher, so look for it in your account.

What decided it: the driver tapped "I'm Here" while still about 1000 m from the pickup point — the record never showed an arrival, and he was never within 200 m of you at any point. Since the no-show conditions weren't met, the fee shouldn't have been charged.

Nothing is required from you. Your account isn't affected.

DRIVER: We reviewed the no-show fee from this trip and it isn't valid. The $6.61 cancellation fee is being refunded to the rider as a Ryde voucher.

What decided it: your "I'm Here" tap was made from roughly 1000 m away from the pickup point, and the record shows no arrival at the pickup — you were never recorded inside the pickup range.

Separately, your account is being sent for review of the "I'm Here" tap made outside the pickup range. Note that repeated no-show disputes found against you may affect your account standing.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7) and send the driver's account for review of the false "I'm Here" tap + flag_account.
ruling.reasoning:
The case enters the NS framework through NS-0: the driver cancelled (F3) and he claims a rider no-show (F11, F12), so the fee's validity is tested by NS-1. [F3][F11][F12][NS-0]

NS-1(i) is satisfied on the record — the timeline shows a driver "I'm Here" tap at 22:37:10 (F5) — but (ii) and (iii) fail. At the moment of the tap the driver was 1000 m from the pickup point (F5), and across the whole trip his closest approach was 868 m (F1), with the platform never recording an arrival (F4). His stationary period of 5 min 5 s was at 993 m from the pickup (F2), and the time he spent inside the 200 m radius after the tap was 0 s (F5). The three NS-1 conditions are cumulative, so the $6.61 no-show fee never became payable. [F1][F2][F4][F5][NS-1]

Because NS-1 fails, NS-2 governs and directs a full refund of the $6.61. The fee amount is taken from the fare record (F7, charged per F3); this is an entitlement dispute, not a billing error, but the entitlement is absent. [F3][F7][NS-1][NS-2]

The driver's chat message "I'm here already ... please come out" at 22:37 (F9) and his written statement that he waited more than three minutes at the pickup (F12) are both contradicted by the GPS and timeline records (F5, F2, F1, F4); system records override statements, and the rider's reply that she was at the pickup point and saw no car (F10) is consistent with those records. [F9][F10][F12][F1][F2][F4][F5][NS-1]

On the account action: the trace records an "I'm Here" tap while GPS placed the driver outside the pickup range (F5, F1), which is exactly the abuse-of-the-cancellation/waiting-button branch that NS-2 attaches `flag_account` to. The driver's two upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F17) do not decide this case — profile facts never decide a case and RD-6 only supplies the accompanying account action — but they reinforce that the flag, not the refund, is where the 90-day history bites. The flag is therefore attached alongside the refund. [F1][F5][F17][NS-2][RD-6]

rejected_claims.reason: The recorded tap at 22:37:10 (F5) only satisfies NS-1(i); NS-1 requires all three conditions, and the same fact fixes the tap 1000 m from the pickup (F5), with no arrival ever logged (F4), so the tap does not make the no-show fee payable [F4][F5][NS-1].

The driver's account of waiting at the pickup (F12) conflicts with the GPS/timeline records placing him stationary 993 m away with 0 s inside the radius (F2, F5), and system records override statements, so the waiting element of NS-1(iii) is not met [F2][F5][F12][NS-1].
This claim is conceded and in fact supports the rider; it is not a ground against the refund, since NS-1(ii) failing triggers NS-2's full refund [F1][F4][F5][NS-1][NS-2].
Conceded and likewise supports the rider; the failure of NS-1(iii) confirms NS-2 applies rather than defeating the claim [F1][F2][F5][NS-1][NS-2].
Not rejected — the driver advocate's own request for a full $6.61 refund (F3, F7) matches the ruling; it is recorded here only as it overlaps the rider's C6 request [F3][F7][NS-2].

certificate: ✓ NS-0 who cancelled [case] cancelled_by = driver (F3)
✓ NS-1 (i) arrival confirmed: driver tapped I'm Here, or the platform auto-confirmed arrival [case] tapped at 22:37:10 (F5)
✗ NS-1 (ii) within 200 m of pickup AT THE MOMENT of the tap [case] 1000 m from pickup when tapped (closest approach overall 868 m) (F5, F1)
✗ NS-1 (iii) stayed at the pickup > 3 min after the tap, until cancelling [case] 0 s continuously inside the radius after the tap (F5)
✓ NS-2 tapped I'm Here while not at pickup → flag_account [case] fake arrival tap (F5, F1)
allowed outcomes: refund_full; amount = cancellation fee $6.61
flag_account required: True

actions.detail: account action is never automatic; queued for Ryde review

what_would_change: Had NS-1 (ii) held ((ii) within 200 m of pickup AT THE MOMENT of the tap), the fee would stand and no refund would be due.
Had NS-1 (iii) held ((iii) stayed at the pickup > 3 min after the tap, until cancelling), the fee would stand and no refund would be due.

claims.assertion: The driver never reached the pickup point: his closest approach was 868 m and he never came within 200 m, which the system records as within_200m false.

He spent the whole waiting period stationary 993 m from the pickup point (22:36:45-22:41:50), and stayed within 200 m of the pickup for 0 seconds after tapping "I'm Here" at 22:37:10, so the NS-1 (iii) waiting test at the pickup point was never met.
Because the driver was not at the pickup point when he tapped "I'm Here" (1000 m away), the NS-1 (ii) requirement fails and the $6.61 no-show fee is not payable by the rider.

The driver's own chat message "I'm here already, silver Toyota Altis, please come out" at 22:37 is contradicted by the GPS record showing he was 1000 m away, and the rider replied that she was at the pickup point and saw no car; statements lose to system records.

The driver's written claim that he "pressed I'm Here and waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" is contradicted by the records: when he pressed the button he was ~1000 m away and his stationary period was 993 m from the pickup point.
The driver cancelled and the $6.61 fee stands on the record even though the conditions for a rider no-show fee were never satisfied, so the full $6.61 must be refunded.

The driver tapped "I'm Here" while GPS placed him outside the pickup point, which is the abuse-of-the-waiting/cancellation-button pattern Ryde flags as fraud, so the account-review flag should be added alongside the refund.

weaknesses: The driver's chat (F9) and written statement (F12) both assert he pressed "I'm Here" and waited more than 3 minutes, and the timeline shows a genuine tap at 22:37:10 (F5); the other side will argue he did wait, ignoring that the GPS record places that tap 1000 m from the pickup.
There is a recorded stationary period of 5 min 5 s (F2), which the driver will present as "waiting for the rider" even though the same fact fixes his position 993 m from the pickup point.
The fare fact F7 confirms $6.61 was actually charged, so the dispute is about entitlement to the fee, not about a billing error; the rider must rely on the NS-1 conditions failing.
The rider's own account has 1 dispute in 90 days with 0 upheld (F16), which the driver side may use to suggest an unmeritorious complaint pattern.

claims.assertion: The driver did press "I'm Here": the timeline records a tap at 22:37:10, and the driver's chat message at 22:37 says he was already at the location.
At the moment of the "I'm Here" tap the GPS places the driver 1000 m from the pickup point and the platform never recorded him at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null), so NS-1(ii) fails.

The driver never entered the 200 m pickup radius at any time: his closest approach was 868 m and he then stayed stationary 993 m away; cumulative time within 200 m after the tap was 0 s, so the >3-minute waiting requirement in NS-1(iii) also fails.
Because the NS-1 conditions are not met, the $6.61 cancellation fee charged to the rider (and recorded in the fare) should be fully refunded to her.

The driver's assertion that he waited at the pickup for more than three minutes is contradicted by the GPS and timeline records, which show him stationary 993 m away, so that statement does not carry the waiting-fee element.

weaknesses: F5 (timeline) does record a driver "I'm Here" tap at 22:37:10, satisfying NS-1(i) on its face, and F11/F9 show the driver communicated in good faith; the rider side will argue this supports a no-show, though it is neutralised by F4, F1 and F2.

The driver has 2 upheld no-show disputes in the last 90 days (F17), which the rider will use to support a flag_account request under NS-2 and to argue this is a pattern rather than a one-off GPS anomaly.

The rider's own profile shows 0 upheld disputes in 90 days (F16), so the rider will be portrayed as a credible, non-abusive complainant; the driver has no system record (other than the null arrival field) proving where he actually believed he was.

points.response: We accept that a tap is recorded at 22:37:10, but NS-1(i) alone is meaningless: the same timeline fact places him 1000 m from the pickup point at that moment, so the tap does not advance the driver's case.
This point is ours, not theirs: a 1000 m tap distance with driver_arrived_at null means NS-1(ii) fails, and under NS-2 the $6.61 must be refunded in full.
Conceded for the rider: never entering the 200 m radius and 0 s inside it after the tap means NS-1(iii)'s >3-minute wait at the pickup point was never served.
We agree the $6.61 cancellation fee recorded on the trip must be fully refunded to the rider; the amount is the fee shown in the fare record.

Agreed, and we go further: the same contradiction plus the "I'm here already" chat message at 22:37 (written while he was 1000 m away) shows the button was asserted deceptively, which supports the additional account flag under NS-2.

The driver's own brief supplies the elements of the account flag: a recorded "I'm Here" tap at a GPS position outside the pickup point, plus 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days, so the refund should be paired with flag_account.

Conceded on the substance: F1 and F4 establish the driver never entered the pickup radius and no arrival was ever recorded. My client's position is that this defeats his own no-show claim, not that the rider is at fault.
Conceded: F2 and F5 fix the stationary period 993 m from the pickup with 0 s inside 200 m, so the NS-1(iii) waiting test at the pickup point cannot be met.
Conceded: F5 shows the "I'm Here" tap at 1000 m from the pickup, so NS-1(ii) fails and the $6.61 no-show fee is not payable, as I already asked in D4 on F3/F7.
Conceded: F9 is a statement and loses to the GPS record F5 and the null arrival field F4; the rider's F10 reply is consistent with the system record.

Conceded: F12 is contradicted by F5 and F2, so the driver's written account of waiting at the pickup cannot stand; my brief D5 already records this. The rider's refund claim follows from the same records.
Conceded: F3 and F7 show the fee was charged although the NS-1 conditions were never satisfied, so the $6.61 must be refunded to the rider under NS-2 — this is the outcome my brief D4 seeks.

This is the rider's strongest point and I do not contest the refund; however, a flag_account under NS-2's fraud branch requires the driver to have tapped "I'm Here" while GPS showed him outside the pickup range, and F17's two upheld no-show disputes are profile facts that under RD-6 cannot decide, only accompany, a finding. I ask the judge to weigh whether a single 1000 m mis-tap by a 5.7-year driver with 1152 trips in 90 days (F17) is the abuse pattern NS-2 targets, rather than treating the flag as automatic.
